Priority Principle: Joint injury

Why Not Others: (b) Walking on the joint causes more damage; (c) Massaging a fresh injury causes more swelling; (d) A hot pack increases the swelling.

PGI Exam Trap: The joint is massaged firmly at once.

5-Second Recall: Rest the joint and apply a cold pack.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cold reduces the swelling of a fresh injury.

question: A nurse on the ward is asked why young children lose heat quickly. Which explanation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: A child has a thick layer of fat under the skin
option_2: A child has a large skin area for the body weight
option_3: A child has a very small skin area
option_4: A child makes a lot of heat from the muscles
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A child has a large skin area for the body weight

Clinical Rationale: A young child has a large skin area for the body weight and loses heat quickly.

Key Clue: why young children lose heat quickly

Priority Principle: Temperature control

Why Not Others: (a) A young child has a thin and not a thick fat layer; (c) The skin area of a child is large for the weight; (d) A young child makes less heat from the muscles.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is left uncovered after a bath.

5-Second Recall: A large skin area loses heat fast.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dry and cover a child quickly.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 4-year-old child on the ward has a head injury and is sleepy. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Give a painkiller and dim the lights
option_2: Let the child sleep without a check
option_3: Check the level of consciousness and report any change
option_4: Give a large meal before the sleep
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Check the level of consciousness and report any change

Clinical Rationale: A sleepy child after a head injury needs the level of consciousness checked and reported.

Key Clue: a sleepy child after a head injury

Priority Principle: Head injury

Why Not Others: (a) A painkiller and dim lights hide the signs; (b) Sleep without a check can hide a serious change; (d) A large meal is not the priority here.

PGI Exam Trap: The sleepy child is left to sleep unchecked.

5-Second Recall: Check the consciousness and report changes.

PNC Exam Pearl: A change in consciousness is the first warning.

question: A nurse on the ward is asked about the rights of a child during care. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The child has a right to comfort and the truth
option_2: The child has no rights during the care
option_3: The parents alone decide and the child is ignored
option_4: The child is too young to be comforted
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The child has a right to comfort and the truth

Clinical Rationale: Every child has a right to comfort and to be told the truth during care.

Key Clue: the rights of a child during care

Priority Principle: Rights of the child

Why Not Others: (b) A child does have rights during the care; (c) The child is not ignored in the decisions; (d) A child of any age can be comforted.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is comforted and told the truth.

5-Second Recall: A child has a right to comfort and the truth.

PNC Exam Pearl: Tell the child the truth in simple words.

question: A nurse on the ward is asked why a child needs a smaller dose of a drug than an adult. Which explanation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The child has a bigger blood volume
option_2: The child has a larger liver than an adult
option_3: The child needs no dose change at all
option_4: The child has a smaller body weight and size
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The child has a smaller body weight and size

Clinical Rationale: A child needs a smaller dose because of the smaller body weight and size.

Key Clue: why a child needs a smaller dose

Priority Principle: Drug dosing in children

Why Not Others: (a) A child has a smaller blood volume; (b) A child does not have a larger liver; (c) The dose does change with the size.

PGI Exam Trap: The adult dose is given to the child.

5-Second Recall: A smaller weight needs a smaller dose.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dose every drug by the weight of the child.

question: A 5-year-old child on the ward has a wound that is red, hot and has pus. Which organism is the MOST likely cause?
option_1: A fungus of the skin
option_2: A virus of the common cold
option_3: Staphylococcus aureus
option_4: A parasite of the gut
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Staphylococcus aureus

Clinical Rationale: A red, hot wound with pus is usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus.

Key Clue: a wound that is red, hot and has pus

Priority Principle: Wound infection

Why Not Others: (a) A skin fungus does not give this picture; (b) A cold virus does not cause a pus wound; (d) A gut parasite does not cause a wound infection.

PGI Exam Trap: A cold virus is blamed for the wound.

5-Second Recall: Staphylococcus aureus infects wounds.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean the wound and give the antibiotic.

question: A nurse on the ward is about to give a drug to a child and must check the five rights. Which list is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Right ward, right bed, right nurse, right file and right day
option_2: Right child, right drug, right dose, right route and right time
option_3: Right drug, right nurse, right shift, right page and right pen
option_4: Right time, right place, right weather, right file and right meal
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Right child, right drug, right dose, right route and right time

Clinical Rationale: The five rights are the right child, drug, dose, route and time.

Key Clue: checking the five rights before a drug

Priority Principle: Medicine safety

Why Not Others: (a) The ward and the bed are not the five rights; (c) The shift and the pen are not the five rights; (d) The weather and the meal are not the five rights.

PGI Exam Trap: The five rights are checked by the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Child, drug, dose, route and time.

PNC Exam Pearl: The five rights prevent a drug error.

question: A nurse on the ward is caring for a 3-year-old child who has had a fit. Which sequence of actions is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Protect the child, time the fit, check the airway and record
option_2: Time the fit, record it, protect the child and check the airway
option_3: Record the fit, protect the child, time it and check the airway
option_4: Check the airway, record the fit, protect the child and time it
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Protect the child, time the fit, check the airway and record

Clinical Rationale: The child is protected, the fit is timed, the airway is checked and the details are recorded.

Key Clue: a child who has had a fit

Priority Principle: Convulsions

Why Not Others: (b) The child is protected before the fit is timed; (c) The child is protected before the fit is timed; (d) The child is protected before the fit is timed.

PGI Exam Trap: The fit is timed before the child is protected.

5-Second Recall: Protect the child and then time the fit.

PNC Exam Pearl: Note the start and the end of the fit.

question: A nurse on the ward is setting up an intravenous infusion for a child. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Set the rate without looking at it
option_2: Check the rate and the settings before starting
option_3: Start the pump with the alarm off
option_4: Leave the pump and check it later
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Check the rate and the settings before starting

Clinical Rationale: The rate and the settings of the infusion are checked before it is started.

Key Clue: setting up an intravenous infusion

Priority Principle: Infusion pump

Why Not Others: (a) The rate is set by checking and not by guess; (c) The alarm is kept on for safety; (d) The pump is not left unchecked.

PGI Exam Trap: The pump is started without a check.

5-Second Recall: Check the rate and the settings.

PNC Exam Pearl: A wrong rate can harm the child.

question: A 5-year-old child on the ward has a low body temperature and is shivering after a long illness. Which action is the FIRST priority?
option_1: Bathe the child in cool water
option_2: Give a cold drink to cool the child
option_3: Dry the child, cover it warmly and check the sugar
option_4: Leave the child uncovered to rest
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Dry the child, cover it warmly and check the sugar

Clinical Rationale: A cold, shivering child is dried, covered warmly and the blood sugar is checked.

Key Clue: a low body temperature with shivering after illness

Priority Principle: Low body temperature

Why Not Others: (a) A cool bath makes the child colder; (b) A cold drink lowers the temperature more; (d) Leaving the child uncovered loses more heat.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is bathed in cool water.

5-Second Recall: Dry and cover the child and check the sugar.

PNC Exam Pearl: Warm the child and check the sugar.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 7-year-old child on the ward has a severe asthma attack with no relief from salbutamol. Which drug is the MOST appropriate to add?
option_1: An antibiotic given into a vein
option_2: An oral antihistamine given at once
option_3: A cough syrup that contains codeine
option_4: A steroid given systemically with ipratropium
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A steroid given systemically with ipratropium

Clinical Rationale: A steroid given systemically with ipratropium is added when salbutamol does NOT relieve the attack.

Key Clue: asthma NOT relieved by salbutamol

Priority Principle: Asthma drugs

Why Not Others: (a) An antibiotic is given only for an infection; (b) An antihistamine does not relieve the tight airways; (c) Codeine can depress the breathing in asthma.

PGI Exam Trap: Salbutamol is repeated without the steroid.

5-Second Recall: Add a systemic steroid with ipratropium.

PNC Exam Pearl: Steroids treat the swelling behind the attack.
